standardColumns.description: The type of user that performed the operation. Possible types are: Admin, System, Application, Service Principal and Other.

standardColumns.name: ActorUserType
standardColumns.description: The type of user that performed the operation. Possible types are: Admin, System, Application, Service Principal and Other.

standardColumns.name: ActorUserId
standardColumns.description: An alternative ID for the user identified in the UserId property. For example, this property is populated with the passport unique ID (PUID) for events performed by users in SharePoint, OneDrive for Business, and Exchange. This property may also specify the same value as the UserID property for events occurring in other services and events performed by system accounts.

standardColumns.name: EventResult
standardColumns.description: Indicates whether the action (specified in the Operation property) was successful or not. Possible values are Succeeded, PartiallySucceeded, or Failed.

standardColumns.name: ObjectId
standardColumns.description: The full path name of the file or folder accessed by the user. For Exchange admin audit logging, the name of the object that was modified by the cmdlet.

standardColumns.name: ActorName
standardColumns.description: The UPN (User Principal Name) of the user who performed the action (specified in the Operation property) that resulted in the record being logged; for example, my_name@my_domain_name. Note that records for activity performed by system accounts (such as SHAREPOINT\system or NT AUTHORITY\SYSTEM) are also included. In SharePoint, another value display in the UserId property is app@sharepoint. This indicates that the "user" who performed the activity was an application that has the necessary permissions in SharePoint to perform organization-wide actions (such as search a SharePoint site or OneDrive account) on behalf of a user, admin, or service. For more information, see the app@sharepoint user in audit records.

standardColumns.description: The IP address of the device that was used when the activity was logged. The IP address is displayed in either an IPv4 or IPv6 address format. For some services, the value displayed in this property might be the IP address for a trusted application (for example, Office on the web apps) calling into the service on behalf of a user and not the IP address of the device used by person who performed the activity. Also, for Azure Active Directory-related events, the IP address isn't logged and the value for the ClientIP property is null.

standardColumns.name: TcpFlagsAck
standardColumns.description: The TCP ACK flag reported. The acknowledgment flag is used to acknowledge the successful receipt of a packet. As we can see from the diagram above, the receiver sends an ACK as well as a SYN in the second step of the three way handshake process to tell the sender that it received its initial packet.

standardColumns.name: TcpFlagsFin
standardColumns.description: The TCP FIN flag reported. The finished flag means there is no more data from the sender. Therefore, it is used in the last packet sent from the sender.

standardColumns.name: TcpFlagsPsh
standardColumns.description: The TCP PSH flag reported. The push flag is somewhat similar to the URG flag and tells the receiver to process these packets as they are received instead of buffering them.

standardColumns.name: TcpFlagsRst
standardColumns.description: The TCP RST flag reported. The reset flag gets sent from the receiver to the sender when a packet is sent to a particular host that was not expecting it.

standardColumns.name: TcpFlagsUrg
standardColumns.description: The TCP URG flag reported. The urgent flag is used to notify the receiver to process the urgent packets before processing all other packets. The receiver will be notified when all known urgent data has been received. See RFC 6093 for more details.

standardColumns.name: TcpFlagsSyn
standardColumns.description: The TCP SYN flag reported. The synchronisation flag is used as a first step in establishing a three way handshake between two hosts. Only the first packet from both the sender and receiver should have this flag set.

standardColumns.description: The GUID for your organization's Office 365 tenant. This value will always be the same for your organization, regardless of the Office 365 service in which it occurs.

standardColumns.description: The type of user that performed the operation. For example: Admin, System, Application, Service Principal, Guest or Other.

standardColumns.name: ActorUserId
standardColumns.description: An alternative ID for the user identified in the UserId property. For example, this property is populated with the passport unique ID (PUID) for events performed by users in SharePoint, OneDrive for Business, and Exchange. This property may also specify the same value as the UserID property for events occurring in other services and events performed by system accounts.

standardColumns.name: EventResult
standardColumns.description: Indicates whether the action (specified in the Operation property) was successful or not. Possible values are Succeeded, PartiallySucceeded, or Failed.

standardColumns.name: ActorName
standardColumns.description: The UPN (User Principal Name) of the user who performed the action (specified in the Operation property) that resulted in the record being logged; for example, my_name@my_domain_name. Note that records for activity performed by system accounts (such as SHAREPOINT\system or NT AUTHORITY\SYSTEM) are also included. In SharePoint, another value display in the UserId property is app@sharepoint. This indicates that the "user" who performed the activity was an application that has the necessary permissions in SharePoint to perform organization-wide actions (such as search a SharePoint site or OneDrive account) on behalf of a user, admin, or service. For more information, see the app@sharepoint user in audit records.

standardColumns.name: SystemNumber
standardColumns.description: The SystemNumber is a two-digit number that identifies a specific SAP system. It is set during the installation of an SAP system and cannot be changed afterwards. standardColumns.name: ClientId
standardColumns.description: The ClientId is a three-digit number that identifies a specific client within an SAP system. The ClientId is used in various SAP transactions and configuration settings to identify the client and ensure that the correct client is being accessed or configured.

standardColumns.name: Instance
standardColumns.description: The Instance refers to a specific installation of an SAP system on a server. An SAP system can have multiple instances running on the same server, each with its own set of processes and resources. The Instance is identified by a unique name that is set during the installation of the SAP system, following syntax: <HOST>_<SYSID>_<SYSNR>.

It helps group similar events together and is used in various transactions and reports to provide information about audit events and to help with auditing and compliance requirements.

standardColumns.name: MonitoringObjectName
standardColumns.description: The MonitoringObjectName is the name of the object being monitored by a specific monitoring activity. It is used in various SAP monitoring tools and reports to provide information about the status and performance of the monitored object.

standardColumns.name: SalTimeChar6

standardColumns.name: MessageText

standardColumns.name: MessageClass
standardColumns.description: The MessageClass is a grouping or category for specific messages or log entries used to organize and classify messages and log entries within an SAP system.

standardColumns.name: MessageContainerId
standardColumns.description: The MessageContainerId is a unique identifier for a specific message container, which is a logical grouping of related messages or log entries within an SAP system.

standardColumns.name: AlertValue
standardColumns.description: The AlertValue represents the importance of the message of a log attribute, characterized by color and severity.

standardColumns.name: AlertSeverity
standardColumns.description: The AlertSeverity is a number between 0 and 255; the larger the number, the greater the severity.

standardColumns.name: AlertSeverityText
standardColumns.description: The AlertSeverityText refers to the text description associated with a specific alert or notification severity level. It provides a detailed explanation of the severity level and is used in various SAP transactions and reports.

standardColumns.name: SentBytes

standardColumns.name: ClientResponseTime
standardColumns.description: Time difference (in seconds) between first byte received from the backend to first byte sent to the client.

standardColumns.name: TimeTaken
standardColumns.description: Length of time (in seconds) that it takes for the first byte of a client request to be processed and its last-byte sent in the response to the client. It's important to note that the Time-Taken field usually includes the time that the request and response packets are traveling over the network.

standardColumns.description: Length of time (in seconds) that it takes for the request to be processed by the WAF.

standardColumns.description: Value can be either Detection or Prevention.

standardColumns.description: Unique identifier to correlate the request received from the client.

standardColumns.name: SslCipher
standardColumns.description: Cipher suite being used for TLS communication (if TLS is enabled).

standardColumns.name: SslProtocol

standardColumns.name: ServerStatus
standardColumns.description: HTTP status code of the backend server.

standardColumns.name: ErrorInfo
standardColumns.description: Error category of the failing request.

standardColumns.name: ServerResponseLatency
standardColumns.description: Latency of the response (in seconds) from the backend server.

standardColumns.name: Host

standardColumns.name: OriginalRequestUriWithArgs
standardColumns.description: This field contains the original request URL.

standardColumns.name: UpstreamSourcePort

standardColumns.name: OriginalHost
standardColumns.description: This field contains the original request host name.

standardColumns.name: Action
standardColumns.description: Action taken on the request. Available values are Blocked and Allowed (for custom rules), Matched (when a rule matches a part of the request), and Detected and Blocked (these are both for mandatory rules, depending on if the WAF is in detection or prevention mode).

standardColumns.name: Site

standardColumns.name: DetailedMessage

standardColumns.name: FileDetails

standardColumns.name: LineDetails
standardColumns.description: Line number in the configuration file that triggered the event.

standardColumns.name: Hostname
standardColumns.description: Hostname or IP address of the Application Gateway.

standardColumns.name: TransactionId

standardColumns.name: CorrelationId

standardColumns.name: Identifier
